title: The almost-done spiral
task: Fix the failing test in calc.py
system: You are a coding agent. Use the tools to change files and run tests. Say done when the tests pass.

script.say: The bug is in add(). Fixing it.

then.say: total() adds 1 for no reason. Removing it.

steps.say: One last change should do it.

incident.why: Here the model stops fixing and starts circling: it turns + 1 into - 1 instead of removing it. Nothing in the loop counts turns, so the same four steps repeat until someone stops the run.
incident.hint: Look at what the model does right after the first failed test run in turn 3.

notes.text: A failing test is useful news, not the failure. Watch what the model does with it.
This is where a person finally stopped the run, 56 turns after it went wrong. Look much earlier.

fixes.text: Give the loop more exits: a turn limit and a token budget
fixes.why: The run stops after a set number of turns or tokens, whatever the model believes.

fixes.text: Tell the model in the prompt to stop when it is stuck
fixes.why: Tempting, but the model already thinks it is almost done. A request in the prompt is not a stop.

fixes.text: Run it again with a stronger model
fixes.why: Any model can circle when the only way out is the model saying it is done.
